name: Chalcolithic Period
shortDesc: Copper Age; early settled agriculture and first urbanization in Mesopotamia and Levant

events.description: Ubaid culture flourishes in Mesopotamia
events.significance: Proto-urban settlements emerge along rivers

events.description: First cities rise at Uruk and Eridu
events.significance: Beginning of urban civilization

events.description: Earliest pictographic writing (proto-cuneiform) at Uruk
events.significance: Humanity's first written records

name: Early Bronze Age
shortDesc: First cities; cuneiform writing; Sumerian city-states; Old Kingdom Egypt; pyramids
biblicalContext: Primordial narratives; Table of Nations; Tower of Babel

events.description: Egypt unified under Narmer/Menes
events.significance: First Egyptian dynasty; start of pharaonic civilization

events.description: Great Pyramid of Giza completed
events.significance: Pinnacle of Old Kingdom engineering

events.description: Sargon of Akkad creates first empire
events.significance: First recorded multi-city empire in history

events.description: Third Dynasty of Ur (Ur III) rises
events.significance: Sumerian renaissance; elaborate temple-ziggurats built

name: Middle Bronze Age
shortDesc: Amorite kingdoms; Old Babylonian Empire; Hyksos in Egypt; Canaanite city-state system
biblicalContext: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph — the Patriarchal period

events.description: Hammurabi becomes king of Babylon
events.significance: Law code promulgated; first written legal system

events.description: Proto-Sinaitic alphabet invented in Sinai/Canaan
events.significance: Ancestor of Hebrew, Greek, and all modern alphabets

events.description: Hyksos seize control of northern Egypt
events.significance: First foreign rulers of Egypt; introduced chariots and bronze weapons

name: Late Bronze Age
shortDesc: Egyptian New Kingdom; Hittite Empire; Amarna international system; widespread trade networks

events.description: Battle of Megiddo — Thutmose III defeats Canaanite coalition
events.significance: Egypt establishes dominance over Canaan

events.description: Akhenaten's religious revolution; worship of Aten
events.significance: First documented monotheistic state religion

events.description: Battle of Kadesh — Egypt vs. Hittites
events.significance: Oldest known peace treaty; Ramesses II and Hattusili III

events.description: Bronze Age Collapse — widespread destruction across the eastern Mediterranean
events.significance: Collapse of major palace economies; Ugarit, Hatti, and Mycenae destroyed

name: Iron Age I
shortDesc: Bronze Age Collapse; Philistine settlement; early Israelite tribal confederacy; Sea Peoples
biblicalContext: Settlement of Canaan; period of the Judges; early monarchy

events.description: Fall of Ugarit; Sea Peoples invade Egypt and Canaan
events.significance: Final blow to Bronze Age palace system

events.description: Philistines capture the Ark of the Covenant at Aphek
events.significance: Crisis that leads to demand for Israelite kingship

events.description: David becomes king of all Israel at Hebron
events.significance: United Monarchy established; Jerusalem conquered

name: Iron Age II
shortDesc: United and Divided Monarchy; Assyrian Empire domination; Neo-Babylonian rise
biblicalContext: Kings of Israel and Judah; major prophets; Assyrian exile

events.description: Kingdom splits into Israel (north) and Judah (south) after Solomon's death
events.significance: Permanent division; two separate biblical kingdoms

events.description: Assyria conquers Samaria; Northern Kingdom of Israel destroyed
events.significance: Ten tribes exiled; 'Lost Tribes of Israel'

events.description: Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem; miraculous deliverance
events.significance: Isaiah's prophecy fulfilled; Hezekiah's tunnel built

name: Babylonian–Persian Period
shortDesc: Babylonian exile; Cyrus Edict (538 BCE); Return to Zion; Second Temple foundation

events.description: Nebuchadnezzar destroys Jerusalem and the First Temple
events.significance: Babylonian exile begins; major theological crisis for Israel

events.description: Cyrus the Great captures Babylon without battle
events.significance: Persian Empire replaces Neo-Babylonian Empire

events.description: Cyrus Edict — Jews permitted to return to Judah
events.significance: End of exile; Isaiah 45 prophecy fulfilled

events.description: Second Temple dedicated in Jerusalem
events.significance: Restoration of Temple worship after 70-year gap
